card.label: King Tomislav Monument
card.text: The bronze equestrian statue that gives the square its name.

king-tomislav-monument.title: King Tomislav Monument, Zagreb | History & Visiting Guide
king-tomislav-monument.description: The King Tomislav Monument on Trg Kralja Tomislava: a bronze equestrian statue by Robert Frangeš-Mihanović, unveiled in 1947. History, facts and the best photo spots.
king-tomislav-monument.intro: At the heart of Trg Kralja Tomislava stands the bronze equestrian monument to Tomislav, the first King of Croatia. Facing the Main Railway Station, it is the square’s defining landmark and the first thing most travellers see when they arrive in Zagreb by train.
king-tomislav-monument.exploreTitle: Explore more on Trg Kralja Tomislava

sections.heading: Who was King Tomislav?
paragraphs: Tomislav was crowned the first King of Croatia in 925, with the blessing of the Pope. He united the Croatian duchies, repelled Magyar invasions and laid the foundations of the medieval Croatian kingdom.
He died around 928 – barely three years after his coronation – and the circumstances of his death remain unknown to this day, feeding centuries of legend.

sections.heading: The sculptor and the statue
paragraphs: The monument was created by the Croatian sculptor Robert Frangeš-Mihanović. He modelled the bronze equestrian statue in 1938, capturing the king on horseback in ceremonial dress.
Because the statue faces the railway station, every arriving traveller meets the king first – a deliberate welcome to the city.

sections.heading: Key facts
items: Unveiled in October 1947, nearly a decade after the sculpture was completed
Commemorates the millennium of the Croatian Kingdom
Made of bronze on a stone pedestal
Located at the southern end of the square, facing Glavni kolodvor (Main Station)
Designed by Robert Frangeš-Mihanović

sections.heading: Symbolism and meaning
paragraphs: The monument was finally unveiled after years of disputes over its design and placement, and after the interruption of the Second World War. For Zagreb, it is a statement of national identity and a tribute to the ruler who gave the country its royal crown.
Together with the yellow Art Pavilion behind it, the statue forms the classic postcard view of the square.

cards.title: Art Pavilion (Umjetnički paviljon)
cards.text: Croatia’s first purpose-built exhibition hall, dating from 1898.

faq.question: Who was King Tomislav?
faq.answer: Tomislav was the first King of Croatia, crowned in 925. He united the Croatian duchies and is considered the founder of the medieval Croatian kingdom.

faq.question: When was the monument unveiled?
faq.answer: The bronze statue was completed in 1938 but unveiled only in October 1947, delayed by disagreements and the Second World War.

faq.question: Who sculpted the King Tomislav Monument?
faq.answer: It was created by the Croatian sculptor Robert Frangeš-Mihanović.

faq.question: Can visitors climb or touch the monument?
faq.answer: No. For preservation and safety, please do not climb on the statue or its pedestal. You can photograph it freely from the surrounding lawns.

faq.question: What is the best spot to photograph the monument?
faq.answer: Stand on the station side of the square at golden hour so the king, the Art Pavilion and the cathedral towers line up in one frame.

things-to-do-near-king-tomislav-square.h1: Things to Do Near King Tomislav Square
things-to-do-near-king-tomislav-square.intro: Trg Kralja Tomislava is the southern gateway to Lenuci’s Green Horseshoe – a chain of parks and squares that makes the Lower Town of Zagreb perfect for walking. From the square you can reach many of the city’s highlights on foot in under 15 minutes.
things-to-do-near-king-tomislav-square.exploreTitle: Explore more on Trg Kralja Tomislava

sections.heading: A natural walking hub
paragraphs: Because the square sits right across from the Main Railway Station and at the start of the Green Horseshoe, it is the ideal starting point for a walking tour of central Zagreb.
Most of the places below are linked by flat, shaded paths and tram lines, so the route works in every season.

cards.title: Zrinjevac Park · 450 m
cards.text: The next green link of the Green Horseshoe, known for plane trees, fountains and a 19th-century meteorological column.

cards.title: Ban Jelačić Square · 850 m
cards.text: Zagreb’s main square and meeting point, with the statue of Ban Josip Jelačić and the start of the shopping street Ilica.

cards.title: Croatian National Theatre (HNK) · 1.1 km
cards.text: A neo-baroque theatre further along the Green Horseshoe, with guided tours and a rich programme.

cards.title: Main Railway Station · opposite
cards.text: The 1892 historicist station building is right across the street – your arrival and departure point.

cards.title: Botanical Garden · 700 m
cards.text: A green oasis with thousands of plant species, ponds and a small glasshouse (seasonal opening).

cards.title: Museum of Arts and Crafts · 1 km
cards.text: One of Zagreb’s most beautiful secessionist buildings, with applied-arts collections.

sections.heading: The Green Horseshoe at a glance
paragraphs: The Green Horseshoe (Zelena potkova) is a U-shaped system of eight squares and parks designed by city planner Milan Lenuci in the late 19th century.
Tomislav Square forms its southern tip; the chain runs north through Zrinjevac to the Botanical Garden and the arts academy.

sections.heading: How to plan your walk
items: Start at the King Tomislav monument and walk north along the Green Horseshoe
Stop at Zrinjevac for its fountains and music pavilion
Continue to Ban Jelačić Square for shopping and trams
Add the Botanical Garden or a museum if time allows

faq.question: How far is Ban Jelačić Square from the square?
faq.answer: About 850 m, an 11-minute walk north through the parks of the Green Horseshoe, or two tram stops on lines 6 or 13.

faq.question: Is everything within walking distance?
faq.answer: Yes. The main nearby sights are 450 m–1.1 km away and connected by flat, pleasant paths.

faq.question: What is the Green Horseshoe?
faq.answer: A chain of eight squares and parks designed by Milan Lenuci in the late 19th century, with Tomislav Square at its southern end.

faq.question: Can I join a guided walking tour?
faq.answer: Many Zagreb city tours covering the Green Horseshoe include Trg Kralja Tomislava in their itinerary.

faq.question: Is the area good for photography?
faq.answer: Yes – the monument, the Art Pavilion and the surrounding historicist architecture make excellent subjects in every season.

green-horseshoe-walking-route.intro: Lenuci’s Green Horseshoe (Zelena potkova) is a U-shaped chain of eight squares and parks laid out by city planner Milan Lenuci in the late 19th century. Starting at Trg Kralja Tomislava, it is one of the easiest and most beautiful city walks in Europe.
green-horseshoe-walking-route.exploreTitle: Explore more on Trg Kralja Tomislava

sections.heading: What is the Green Horseshoe?
paragraphs: The Horseshoe connects the green spaces of the Lower Town into a continuous park system, balancing the built-up blocks of central Zagreb.

Its eight squares and parks include Tomislavov trg, Zrinjevac, Strossmayerov trg, the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts (HAZU), the Botanical Garden, Markušev trg, Trg žrtava fašizma and Nikola Šubić Zrinski Square.

sections.heading: Squares and parks along the route
items: Tomislavov trg – the southern gateway, with the King Tomislav monument
Zrinjevac – fountains, plane trees and a music pavilion
Strossmayerov trg – framed by the Croatian Academy and the Archaeological Museum
Botanical Garden – a quiet green oasis with ponds
Markušev trg and Trg žrtava fašizma – elegant residential squares
Zrinski and Petar Preradović Squares – closing the northern arm

sections.heading: Suggested self-guided route
paragraphs: Begin at the King Tomislav monument facing the Main Station. Walk north along the lawns, cross to Zrinjevac, then continue through Strossmayerov trg to the Botanical Garden.
The full loop is about 2 km and takes 45–60 minutes at a relaxed pace, longer if you stop at museums and cafés.

cards.title: Zrinjevac music pavilion
cards.text: A favourite spot for open-air concerts and seasonal decorations.

cards.title: HAZU and the academies
cards.text: The neo-baroque academy building anchors the eastern side of the Horseshoe.

cards.title: Botanical Garden glasshouse
cards.text: A small historic glasshouse amid thousands of plant species.

faq.question: How long is the Green Horseshoe walk?
faq.answer: The full loop is about 2 km and takes roughly 45–60 minutes at a relaxed pace.

faq.question: Where does the route start?
faq.answer: At Trg Kralja Tomislava (Tomislav Square), right across from the Main Railway Station.

faq.question: Is the Green Horseshoe free to visit?
faq.answer: Yes. All the squares and parks are public spaces, free and open at all times.

faq.question: Is the route wheelchair and pram friendly?
faq.answer: Yes. The paths are flat and paved throughout the Lower Town.

faq.question: When is the best time to walk it?
faq.answer: Spring and early autumn for flowers and mild weather; winter for the Advent decorations along the route.

card.label: Advent in Zagreb
card.text: The square hosts Zagreb’s Ice Park during the award-winning Advent season.

advent-king-tomislav-square.description: During Advent in Zagreb, Trg Kralja Tomislava hosts the Ice Park – a festive open-air skating rink. Dates, tips and what to expect at Zagreb’s Christmas market.
advent-king-tomislav-square.h1: Advent in Zagreb at King Tomislav Square
advent-king-tomislav-square.intro: Every winter, Zagreb transforms into one of Europe’s most beloved Christmas destinations. Trg Kralja Tomislava plays a central role: the square becomes home to the Zagreb Ice Park, a large open-air skating rink wrapped in festive lights.
advent-king-tomislav-square.exploreTitle: Explore more on Trg Kralja Tomislava

sections.heading: Why Advent in Zagreb is famous
paragraphs: Advent in Zagreb has been voted the best Christmas market in Europe by European Best Destinations (in 2016, 2017 and 2018).
The city fills with lights, wooden stalls, concerts and the scent of mulled wine from late November to early January.

sections.heading: The Ice Park on Tomislav Square
paragraphs: During Advent, the square is converted into an outdoor skating rink – the Ice Park (Klizalište) – with skaters gliding beneath the King Tomislav monument.
The Art Pavilion glows behind the festive lights, making it one of the most photographed spots of the season.

sections.heading: What to expect
items: Outdoor ice skating for all ages
Festive lights and a tall Christmas tree
Food and drink stalls with local specialities and mulled wine
Live music and weekend concerts
Easy access from the Main Station, just across the street

sections.heading: Tips for visiting
paragraphs: Dress warmly and wear gloves; skating sessions can be cold. Buy tickets online to skip the queue.
Combine the square with other Advent locations – Ban Jelačić Square, Zrinjevac and European Square – all within a short walk.
Visit in the evening for the full light display, but expect larger crowds on weekends.

faq.question: When is Advent in Zagreb held?
faq.answer: Typically from late November to early January. Exact dates change each year, so check the official Advent in Zagreb programme.

faq.question: Is the Ice Park really on this square?
faq.answer: Yes. During Advent, Trg Kralja Tomislava hosts the Zagreb Ice Park, a large open-air skating rink.

faq.question: Do I need tickets for the Ice Park?
faq.answer: Skating usually requires a ticket or session pass; some sessions are free for children. Buy online to avoid queues.

faq.question: Is the square accessible during Advent?
faq.answer: Yes. The square stays open to pedestrians and is step-free from the Main Station.

faq.question: What are the opening hours during Advent?
faq.answer: Stalls and the rink generally run from late morning to late evening. Check the official programme for current hours.
